body.objective: Students will be able to greet and introduce myself.
body.iCan: I can greet and introduce myself.
successCriteria: I can greet people and say goodbye in French
I can introduce myself with my name, age and where I live
I can ask someone their name and age
body.hook: Over 10 million people in Canada can speak French, and there are francophone communities right here in Alberta, from Edmonton's Bonnie Doon neighbourhood to Saint-Paul, Falher and Bonnyville. The first thing you'll do in any of those places is greet someone and introduce yourself. Today, you'll learn how.

vocabulary.definition: Hello / good morning (polite, used all day).
I am … years old (literally "I have … years").

study.title: Enchanté !
study.question: How do I greet and introduce myself in French?
study.passage:
Dialogue (read aloud with a partner):
Léa : Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Léa. Comment t'appelles-tu ?
Omar : Salut, Léa ! Je m'appelle Omar.
Léa : Enchantée, Omar. Quel âge as-tu ?
Omar : J'ai douze ans. Et toi ?
Léa : Moi, j'ai treize ans. Où habites-tu ?
Omar : J'habite à Calgary. Et toi ?
Léa : J'habite à Edmonton.
Omar : Super ! Au revoir, Léa !
Léa : À bientôt !
English support: Enchanté(e) = pleased to meet you (add -e if you are female). Et toi ? = And you? À bientôt = See you soon.
Numbers for ages: onze (11), douze (12), treize (13), quatorze (14), quinze (15).
Tu or vous? Use tu with friends, family and other young people. Use vous with adults you don't know well, teachers and in formal situations: "Comment vous appelez-vous ?"
Culture note: In Quebec and some francophone communities, friends often greet with "la bise," a light kiss on each cheek; in school in Alberta, a handshake or a wave is common.
study.source: Original dialogue written for this lesson.
steps: Listen to and repeat the dialogue
Learn to say your age with avoir
Role-play the dialogue with your own information
Introduce your partner to another pair
discussion: Why does French say "J'ai douze ans" (I have twelve years) instead of "I am"?

What is the difference between Bonjour and Salut?
Why does Léa say "Enchantée" with an extra -e?
study.product: Write and perform a short dialogue (6–8 lines) where you meet a new student, greet them, ask their name, age and where they live, and say goodbye.

body.objective: Students will be able to describe people with adjectives.
body.iCan: I can describe people with adjectives.
successCriteria: I can describe people using il est and elle est
I can make adjectives agree with masculine and feminine nouns
I can describe myself and a friend in French
body.hook: Imagine describing your best friend to someone who's never met them. In French, the words you use (tall, funny, kind) change shape to match the person. Today you'll learn to describe people with être and adjectives.

study.title: Qui est-ce ?
study.question: How do I describe people in French?
study.passage:
Text (read aloud):
Voici mon ami Karim. Il est grand et sportif. Il est très drôle !
Voici mon amie Chloé. Elle est petite et intelligente. Elle est gentille, mais un peu timide.
Et moi ? Je suis grand et un peu timide. Je ne suis pas sportif, mais je suis drôle !
Grammar: être (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, elle est.
Adjective agreement: for a feminine person, add -e (grand → grande). If the adjective already ends in -e, no change (drôle, timide). Some change more: gentil → gentille, sportif → sportive.
Negative: ne … pas goes around the verb: Je ne suis pas timide.
Activity: "Qui est-ce ?": describe a classmate or a famous person with three adjectives; the class guesses who it is.
study.source: Original text written for this lesson.
discussion: Why does grand become grande for Chloé?
How do you make a sentence negative?
study.product: Write five sentences describing yourself and a friend using at least six adjectives with correct agreement and one negative sentence.

body.objective: Students will be able to ask and answer personal questions.
body.iCan: I can ask and answer personal questions.
successCriteria: I can ask personal questions in French
I can answer with full sentences
I can hold a short getting-to-know-you conversation
body.hook: Getting to know someone in French means asking questions: Where do you live? What do you like? Do you have brothers or sisters? Today you'll ask and answer the questions people ask on a first meeting.

vocabulary.term: Tu as des frères ou des sœurs ?
vocabulary.definition: Do you have brothers or sisters?
I have a brother / a sister

study.title: Faisons connaissance
study.question: How do I ask and answer personal questions?
study.passage:
Dialogue (read with a partner):
Nadia : Salut ! Tu es d'où ?
Lucas : Je viens de Montréal, mais j'habite à Edmonton maintenant. Et toi ?
Nadia : Je viens du Liban. J'habite à Calgary. Tu as des frères ou des sœurs ?
Lucas : Oui, j'ai un frère et une sœur. Et toi ?
Nadia : Non, je n'ai pas de frères ni de sœurs. Je suis fille unique.
Lucas : Qu'est-ce que tu aimes ?
Nadia : J'aime le soccer et la musique. Et toi ?
Lucas : Moi, j'aime les jeux vidéo !
Grammar: avoir (to have): j'ai, tu as, il a, elle a. After a negative, un/une/des become de: J'ai un frère → Je n'ai pas de frère.
Three ways to ask a question: rising intonation (Tu as un chien ?), est-ce que (Est-ce que tu as un chien ?), inversion (As-tu un chien ?).
Activity: interview three classmates and record their answers in a chart.
study.source: Original dialogue written for this lesson.
steps: Read the dialogue with a partner
